description: Athlete running 32 miles/week but 60% of it is Z3 — junk miles that fatigue without building aerobic base. 18 weeks to a half marathon. Dean must name the aerobic efficiency problem specifically, not describe the data back.

ground_truth.notes:
Sarah has been running 32mi/week for months but 60% of it is in Z3 — the aerobic efficiency problem. Z3 is too hard to be truly aerobic recovery/base building, but too easy to be genuine quality training. It sits in the gray zone that builds fatigue without the training adaptations of either Z2 base work OR Z4/Z5 quality work.

For an 18-week half marathon build, this is the central issue. With 18 weeks she has plenty of time to fix it, but Dean needs to name the actual problem:

Correct behavior:
1. Use the actual numbers: 60% Z3, 32mi/week, 18 weeks
2. Name what Z3-dominant training means in practice: fatiguing without building aerobic base — the mileage is there but the physiological adaptation isn't
3. Say what will change: shifting Z3 miles to true easy (Z1/Z2) plus adding one genuine quality session
4. Close with the injury question

Do NOT:
- Say 'solid base', 'great foundation', 'consistent mileage'
- Just describe the data back ('I can see you've been running 5 days a week at about 32 miles')
- Be vague about the problem ('we'll want to work on your effort distribution')
- Suggest the mileage is fine as-is
- Mention that 18 weeks is plenty of time without connecting it to what will happen in those 18 weeks

Bonus credit: mention that the 2:02 half gives a target — the training zones from that PR will be used to set her easy pace.
